name: Magic Hair Growth products from Indian pharmacy (Himalaya)

lead: Himalaya is an Indian company founded in 1930 that sells Ayurvedic and herbal healthcare and personal-care products. Some of its hair-care lines are used by people looking for fuller-looking hair.
The entry covers such herbal hair-growth products sold through Indian pharmacies. Support comes from user belief in Ayurvedic herbs rather than published trials of a named product.

paras: Products are typically topical herbal oils, shampoos and creams applied to the scalp as part of a routine, and are sold over the counter.
Herbal does not exclude irritation or allergy. The company has also been in public dispute with a critic over claims about its products.

chain: Claimed support for the hair cycle
angle.text: Users apply herbal oils or creams to the scalp expecting thicker hair over weeks to months.

lead: The Himalaya Wellness Company was founded in Dehradun in 1930 and now sells pharmaceuticals, personal care and nutrition products in over 100 countries, with a range built on Ayurvedic ingredients.[1] Users looking for hair-growth help sometimes buy its herbal hair-care products from Indian pharmacies, hoping for thicker-looking hair.
The company states it employs many researchers working on Ayurvedic herbs and minerals.[1] No published clinical trial of a specific Himalaya hair-growth product was loaded for this entry.

paras: Founder Mohammad Manal began commercialising Ayurvedic products in 1930; the company moved to Bombay in the 1950s and launched Liv.52 in 1955, entered the US in 1996, and was reported selling in 106 countries.[1]

In September 2023 the company obtained an injunction from a Bangalore court against Cyriac Abby Philips, a critic of alternative medicine, which commentators called excessive; the Karnataka High Court ordered his account reinstated in October 2023.[1]
